claim: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3, with m=min D, gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=3+min{1/4,2/m}, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k, all sufficiently large integers are sums of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.

quadruple.statement: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3, with m=min D, gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=3+min{1/4,2/m}, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k, all sufficiently large integers are sums of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.
quadruple.stage: Finite sets of integer bases, countable locally finite labelled power occurrences, exact rational reciprocal mass, and finite subset sums in the integers.

shape.objects: Inputs are arbitrary finite D, positive k and finite occurrence deletions F; outputs are finite occurrence subsets for each sufficiently large n. Finite base partitions are built by adjoining unused bases to a gcd-one seed, and disjoint finite occurrence subsets combine by union. All integers, rational sums, finite sets, pairs and functions have core Lean or Mathlib definitions. Finite selections can be random variables, but no spread estimate is recorded.
shape.quantifiers: For every such finite D, every positive integer k and every finite labelled deletion F, there exists N(D,k,F), for every integer n>=N there is a finite subset of the remaining labels whose values sum to n. Leading quantifiers are universal over countably encoded inputs; this is covering, not a full-measure assertion.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no eventual-coverage assertion at the exact stated reciprocal threshold. It is not an optimization problem for that threshold. An unspecified finite N(D,k,F) settles the claim; no explicit quantitative bound on N is requested.
shape.ambient_structure: Order and divisibility coexist with labelled finite-set union and addition. Combining disjoint occurrence supports adds their sums, permitting a finite interval to amplify against a bounded-gap remainder. Exact per-base geometric sums and finite cyclic residue groups retain the pure-power structure. No random-event dependence estimate or density-increment piece system is supplied.
shape.symmetries: Permuting labels within equal numerical values preserves availability; arbitrary numerical deduplication does not. Disjoint-support union is the additive operation. Translation or dilation of D does not preserve the hypotheses, and no closed density-increment system is asserted.
shape.configuration: Every sufficiently large n must be a positive sum using each allowed pair (d,j) at most once. Finite prefixes need not be complete, and arbitrary restriction to a base subfamily can destroy both reciprocal mass and gcd one. Any finite-correction amplification must keep its correction labels disjoint from the reserved bounded-gap supply.
shape.extremal_candidate: No optimal reciprocal threshold or minimum certificate is claimed. The candidate is a feasible three-way partition whose first two components have mass at least one and strictly below9/8, with the gcd-one minimum-preserving component used for correction.
shape.finite_certificates: The proved finite allocation verifies the accepted three-component criterion for the exact admitted range. The inherited terminating interval search from acceptance-000005 supplies a finite seed, with gap length computed after correction-label removal, and a terminating disjoint-support representation search. No mathematical process has been executed.
shape.monotonicity: Representability is preserved by adding unused labels and can only be lost by increasing k or deleting more labels. The positive cutoff starts at k=1. The proposed threshold is no worse than the accepted3+2/m bound; its exact lower-mass complement remains open, with no fixed finite prefix deciding it.
shape.uniformity_parameter: All finite D, arbitrarily large minimum and cardinality, every positive cutoff k and every finite deletion F. The representation threshold may depend on all three inputs.
shape.proof_shape: An analytical proof candidate is recorded in moves/001-quarter-mass-completeness.md. It audits accepted three-component amplification, proves a uniform gcd-one core of mass below9/8 by gcd descent and exhaustive small-base cases, constructs a disjoint second bin below9/8, proves the third mass exceeds one at13/4, and combines that theorem with the accepted3+2/m bound for m>=8. Every quantifier and inherited intermediate criterion is explicit; independent result acceptance is pending.
shape.neighbours: Known true locally: the occurrence-preserving three-component criterion, all-cutoff/deletion estimates, and threshold3+2/m at checkpoint-000016, acceptance-000005; the core-selection construction at acceptance-000001. Known false: generic strong-profile and signed-profile central-seed inferences, acceptances000003/4, not pure-power counterexamples. The original root and the new complementary range are open. Finite allocation patterns are checkable neighbours. No verbatim simpler ambient or property-reflecting correspondence is recorded.
shape.known_bounds: The accepted previous threshold is3+2/m. This attack now has a computer-free proof candidate for3+min{1/4,2/m}, including equality, all positive cutoffs and finite deletions. New finite lemmas give a minimum-preserving gcd-one core in[1,9/8) and a second increasing first-crossing bin in[1,9/8). The new theorem is not yet independently accepted. The original threshold-one assertion remains open; no optimal constant, uniform N, empirical search, or formal certificate is claimed.
shape.missing_input: No unproved mathematical input remains in the local analytical proof candidate. Independent result review and immutable acceptance are still required. The original root and complementary lower-mass range remain open; this does not supply their missing integer seed.
shape.base_theory: Classical arithmetic, real analysis and compact-group arguments in ZFC with choice. No additional axiom, forcing principle, guessing principle or uncountable independence hypothesis is used. These objects and any finite rational or residue checks lie within Lean's standard classical axioms, but no formal verification or mathematical computation is admitted.
